Definition: diminutive of G5043; an infant, i.e. (plural figuratively) darlings (Christian converts):--little children.
BiblicalUsage: The word is little children, John's tender name for his readers. He writes, My little children, these things write I unto you, that ye sin not, and if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father. He says, Little children, let no man deceive you, and, Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome them, because greater is He that is in you. Jesus Himself uses it at the supper: Little children, yet a little while I am with you.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe little children is the name of belonging: John writes to them as a father, and Jesus calls His own by it at the last supper. My position is that the church is a family before it is anything else, and the little ones are the ones He keeps.
